Modify or Extend Existing RTL: When extending existing DSP RTL for new control/FSM requirements, first satisfy interface/visibility contracts used by verification (new params/ports and probe-friendly packed signals), then align cycle-by-cycle internal buffering/state updates to the checker’s reference model before optimizing behavior.
Integrate multiple modules into a top mo: For top-level wrapper tasks, first satisfy required source filenames/modules, then implement minimal glue logic that computes checker-visible outputs directly from post-processed submodule outputs while propagating critical submodule error flags.
Create new RTL from spec: When testbench edge sampling is strict, align output-valid timing to the checker’s observed cycle semantics and keep throughput counters tied to accepted input-valid events for stable parameter-sweep passes.
Debug/fix buggy RTL: For 2-way cache debug tasks, implement explicit per-way tag/data/valid/dirty state with deterministic hit selection and expose victim-way state so replacement and observability checks both pass.
